exposure: Pulse oximetry (pre- and post-ductal SpO2 measurements)
cohort: Hemodynamically stable neonates born in a tertiary hospital in India, excluding those with antenatally diagnosed cardiac anomalies, outborn neonates, unwilling parents/guardians, or sick neonates with SpO2 <90% at birth.
finding: Pulse oximetry was found to be a reliable and feasible screening tool for CHD in neonates, with an SpO2 cutoff value of ≤90% demonstrating 90% sensitivity, 99.94% specificity, 75% positive predictive value, and 99.98% negative predictive value for detecting CCHD.
followup_time: Within the first few days of life (initial screening after 24 hours of life, with repeat SpO2 and echocardiography as needed)
cross-section timing: After 24 hours of life for initial screening.
gest_age: Majority (89.2%) were term (≥37 weeks), with 10.8% being preterm (<37 weeks).
